chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who reported it, he said:

Indeed, when a man marries a woman by Mut'ah, there is upon her a waiting period for others. So when he intends to marry her, there is not upon her from him a waiting period; he can marry her whenever he desires.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies a specific nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding temporary marriage (Mut'ah), distinguishing between the general waiting period for remarriage to others and the exemption from waiting for the original husband. It highlights the flexibility of Mut'ah contracts, where the dissolution does not impose a barrier to immediate re-contracting between the same parties, reflecting the distinct legal status of Mut'ah compared to permanent marriage. This ruling is foundational in understanding the practical application of 'Iddah as recorded in al-Kafi.
